### Overview
There has never been a more important or exciting time to study the mediated world.

This course builds your understanding of the changing contexts of media and communication practices. You will gain insight into the key issues affecting the communications and media industries and you will examine these developments from cultural, political and theoretical perspectives. You will be challenged to communicate your new knowledge and insights with impact and purpose, accommodating a range of media formats and potential audiences.

This course develops an advanced understanding of the contemporary communications and media environment. It is suitable for those pursuing careers in a wide range of communications and media roles, including in the areas of communications, media relations, social media, digital engagement, public policy and public relations.

You will have the opportunity to engage with local practitioners and industry experts via guest speakers, case studies, internships and site visits. You will also have the opportunity to conduct in-depth analysis of contemporary media industries, issues and organisations.

### Course intended learning outcomes
On successful completion you will be able to:
**1.**
investigate challenges and opportunities for the communications and media industries and assess their impacts on wider contexts, including culture, politics, business, and everyday life;
**2.**
work effectively, thoughtfully and professionally as peers and team members, able to lead, collaborate and critique;
**3.**
undertake advanced independent research employing research methodologies and ethics.
**4.**
critically analyse and reflect on important trends, issues and challenges shaping the contemporary communications and media environment;
**5.**
skilfully communicate insights into the communications and media industries to a range of specialist and non-specialist audiences in written, verbal and media formats;

### AHEGS
The Master of Communications and Media Studies is a postgraduate course. It is taught in English and normally takes two years of full-time study or four years of part-time study. The course focuses on challenges posed by the emergence of digital media, globalisation and increasing levels of cross-cultural exchange. Graduates will demonstrate a sound knowledge of diverse aspects of communication and media including policy, content and technology change and will articulate and apply an understanding of the world view of communications and media as it applies to politics, public administration and business. The Master of Communications and Media Studies is a Level 9 Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) qualification. The minimum requirements for admission are set out in the Monash University (Academic Board) Regulations.

## Master of Cultural and Creative Industries
##### A6004

### Overview
The Masters of Cultural and Creative Industries will prepare you for diverse career pathways in the cultural sector. The course examines the trends and transformation of the global cultural and creative industries and multi-faceted challenges facing creative practitioners, cultural managers, creative entrepreneurs and producers, and policymakers. The course draws on research and teaching expertise from Monash academics in cross-disciplinary areas of cultural management, cultural policy, film and media studies, cultural economics and strategic communication. Situated within Melbourne, the cultural hub of Australia, the course offers opportunities for industry internships and field trips if you are seeking an immersive experience in Melbourne's vibrant cultural and creative sector.

Graduates of our Master of Cultural and Creative Industries have gone on to pursue careers in the public and private cultural sector, such as:

  * Business development manager

  * Public relations manager

  * Creative marketer including social media content maker

  * Project manager for events

  * Arts administrators

  * Arts programming director

  * Community engagement and visitor experience officer

### Structure
The course is structured in four parts: Part A Core studies, Part B. Applied Studies, Part C. Professional practice studies and Part D. Elective studies.  

A research pathway is also available subject to meeting eligibility requirements.

Part A. Core studies

These studies provide you with foundation knowledge and skills in the field of cultural and creative industries at a graduate level. They will immerse you in cultural and creative industries studies and provide you with the opportunity to apply specialised understanding of the field in real world settings. They draw on best practices within the broad field of cultural and creative industries studies practice and research to further your understanding of the complex ecosystem in which cultural and economic goals and dynamics combine in ways that transgress traditional disciplinary and policy boundaries.

Part B. Applied studies

The focus of these studies is professional or scholarly work that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development.

Part C. Professional practice studies

Designed in association with industry experts, select from this suite of professional enhancement offerings to build essential competencies for your career pathway.

Part D. Elective studies

Select from a range of options designed to enhance specific knowledge and skills in Cultural and Creative Industries and related fields. Units not taken in Part A and Part B are also available as elective options.

Master's entry points

Depending on prior qualifications you may receive entry level credit (a form of block credit) which determines your point of entry to the course. 

  * If you are admitted at entry level 1 you complete 96 credit points, comprising Part. A, Part. B, Part. C and Part. D. 
  * If you are admitted at entry level 2 you complete 72 credit points, comprising Part. A, Part. B, Part. C (6 credit points) and Part. D (12 credit points).
  * If you are admitted at entry level 3 you complete 48 credit points, comprising Part. A (36 credit points) and Part. B.

Note: Students eligible for credit for prior studies may elect not to receive the credit and complete one of the higher credit-point options.

Course progression maps

The course progression map provides guidance on unit enrolment for each semester of study.

If you are eligible to enrol in the 1.5-year entry point, you have the option of completing this course intensively over a 12-month period by following the intensive course progression map.

investigate a range of distinct practical challenges in the field, and related policy development and implementation, using case studies and fieldwork;

**3.**
conceptualise contemporary challenges and opportunities for cultural and creative industries, from individual practices to large-scale cultural projects, situated in a wider international context;
**4.**
skilfully and appropriately communicate ideas to a variety of audiences (academic, policy, industry, and community), verbally and in writing;

### AHEGS
The Master of Cultural and Creative Industries is a postgraduate course. It is taught in English. The course normally takes two years of full-time study or part-time equivalent to complete. The course includes study of the structures and dynamics of creative industries, creative cities, contemporary arts practices, and culture economy and culture and sustainable development. Graduates will display a high level of written and oral communication skills to a variety of audiences and apply independent research skills to identify and investigate concrete challenges and issues in creative businesses and policy development and implementation. The Master of Cultural and Creative Industries is a Level 9 Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) qualification. The minimum requirements for admission are set out in the Monash University (Academic Board) Regulations.

## Master of International Development Practice
##### A6006
##### 96 credit points
You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
Equitable and sustainable human development remains a pressing global concern. Complex socio-political, health, economic, cultural, humanitarian, and ecological challenges contribute to extreme poverty, reduced human development, fragile governance and environmental vulnerability affecting the well-being of millions of people worldwide. These complex, multidimensional challenges require adaptable professionals with the practical skills and analytical capacity to strategically and ethically address them at community, national and global levels. Our graduates can adapt rapidly to changing circumstances while understanding that at the core of development practice are enduring principles of social justice, equity, inclusion, and sustainability

The Master of International Development Practice offers a multi-disciplinary, applied approach to the theory and practice of sustainable human development. Delivered by specialists across the humanities and social sciences, medicine, business and economics, education and law Faculties, the program delivers rigorous research training alongside the critical and practical skills of project design and management and leadership skills. 

You may choose to focus your electives in one of the following areas:

  * democracy, justice and governance

  * gender, peace and security

  * crisis, change management and leadership

  * sustainable resource management

  * sustainable economies

  * Leading in multicultural and intercultural contexts

Opportunities for fieldwork, study abroad and internship engagement include options to engage in field-schools. 

Graduate employment opportunities may include local and international non-government organisations, human rights advocacy, aid agencies, government, social enterprise, corporate social responsibility, the business sector, universities, community organisations, and international institutions such as the United Nations,  World Bank and International Migration Organisation.

### Structure
The course is structured in four parts. Part A. Core studies, Part B. Applied studies, Part C. Professional practice studies, Part D. Elective studies. 

A research pathway is also available subject to meeting eligibility requirements.

Part A. Core studies 

These studies will immerse you in international development practice at graduate level and draw on best practices within the broad realm of international development theory, practice and research to address questions ranging from the causes of inequality and disparity, evolving aid and development thought and practice, to the impact of politics, economics, culture, history and natural resources human development.

Part B. Applied studies  

The focus of these studies is professional or scholarly work that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development.

Part C. Professional practice studies

Designed in association with industry experts, select from this suite of professional enhancement offerings to build essential competencies for your career pathway

Part D. Elective studies 

Select from a range of options designed to enhance specific knowledge and skills in international development practice and related fields.

Master's entry points

Depending on prior qualifications you may receive entry level credit (a form of block credit) which determines your point of entry to the course: 

  * If you are admitted at entry level 1, you complete 96 credit points, comprising Part A, Part B, Part C and Part D.
  * If you are admitted at entry level 2, you complete 72 credit points, comprising Part A, Part B, Part C (6 credit points), Part. D (18 credit points).
  * If you are admitted at entry level 3, you complete 48 credit  points, comprising Part A and Part B.

Note: Students eligible for credit for prior studies may elect not to receive the credit and complete one of the higher credit-point options.

### Course intended learning outcomes
On successful completion you will be able to:
**1.**
communicate research findings effectively and perceptively in a range of formats to a variety of audiences.
**2.**
critically analyse the political, economic, cultural and environmental challenges contributing to human inequalities;
**3.**
employ ethics research methodology to plan and conduct an independent research project;
**4.**
critically appraise the range of organisations and institutions involved in international development, their working culture and funding processes;
**5.**
apply theoretical learning and best practice within the broad professional and practical context  of international development practice, policy, governance and research;
**6.**
explain and evaluate complex sustainable development challenges and debates across diverse cultural and geo-political contexts;

### Progression to further studies
Successful completion of this course may provide a pathway to a graduate research degree if you complete the research pathway.

Master's accelerated pathway

### AHEGS
The Master of International Development Practice is a postgraduate course. It is taught in English and normally takes two years of full-time study or four years of part-time study. The course offers a multi-disciplinary applied approach to the theory and practice of sustainable development through research training, project management and leadership skills development within an interdisciplinary curriculum. Graduates will demonstrate a critical understanding of the political, economic, cultural and environmental challenges contributing to human inequalities and be able to articulate and apply knowledge of best practice within the broad realm of international development practice, policy, governance and research. The Master of International Development Practice is a Level 9 Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) qualification. The minimum requirements for admission are set out in the Monash University (Academic Board) Regulations.

### Degrees awarded
Master of International Development Practice

## Master of Interpreting and Translation Studies
##### A6007
##### 96 credit points
You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
The Master of Interpreting and Translation Studies is aimed at students with advanced bilingual proficiency and seeks to develop your skills in translation and interpreting from/to English and another language, and your awareness of practical and theoretical approaches to translation/interpreting practice and studies. The course offers two specialisations, focusing on:

  * Translation (Chinese, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish)

  * Interpreting and translation (Chinese, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish).

Note: Languages on offer in any one year may vary depending on student enrolments.

You will gain a foundation in theories of translation and interpreting and receive training in research in the field. Upon completion of this course, you will be able to conceptualise translation/interpreting studies as an academic discipline in its historical, cross-disciplinary and intercultural context.

Note: Online delivery is available to domestic students in the translation-only specialisation

### Structure
The course is structured in five parts: Part A. Foundation studies, Part B. Core studies, Part C. Applied studies, Part D. Professional practice studies, and Part E. Elective studies.

Part A. Foundation studies

The focus of these studies is the theory and practice of translation and interpreting, familiarising you with current research models and methodologies in translation studies.

Part B. Core studies

These studies draw on best practices within interpreting and translation fields, providing intensive language-specific practice in written and oral transfer skills at a level required for certification by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters (NAATI). In addition to the relevant theoretical frameworks, the core units will also provide you with the discourse analysis, ethical and professional frameworks that are essential for professional interpreting and translation practice.

Part C. Applied studies

The focus of these studies is professional or scholarly work that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development or a research pathway. Students in the interpreting and translation specialisation will also develop advanced skills in specialised fields of interpreting.

Part D. Professional practice studies

Designed in association with industry experts, select from this suite of professional enhancement offerings to build essential competencies for your career pathway.

Part E. Elective studies

Select from a range of options designed to enhance specific knowledge and skills in interpreting and translation and related fields, including a suite of professional enhancement offerings to build essential competencies for your career pathway.

Depending on prior qualifications you may receive entry level credit (a form of block credit) which determines your point of entry to the course.

On successful completion you will be able to:

critically analyse, evaluate, and engage with key texts and cultural products pertaining to the theoretical field of interpreting and translation studies.

apply and communicate knowledge of global best practice in interpretation and translation in diverse and collaborative professional contexts
**3.**
translate and interpret spoken and written language in English and another language at an advanced level, applying ethical practice commensurate with professional certification

### AHEGS
The Master of Interpreting and Translation Studies is a postgraduate course. It is taught in English and normally takes two years of full-time study or four years of part-time study. Graduates will be able to demonstrate advanced skills in translation and interpreting from/to English and another language and awareness of practical and theoretical approaches to translating/interpreting practice suitable for accreditation. In addition to advanced analytical and communication skills they will demonstrate a thorough understanding of research methodology and ethics. The minimum requirements for admission are set out in the Monash University (Academic Board) Regulations.

Graduates will have achieved intensive language-specific practice in written and oral transfer skills to standards set by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters (NAATI).

## Master of Journalism

### Overview
In a global landscape with competing voices, misinformation and reactive news cycles, only experts and innovators can cut through and make media that matters. A Master of Journalism at Monash University is more than a postgraduate career qualification. We are creating the leaders of journalism for the new wave of media, as well as developing critical communication skills for other careers.

Journalism teaches you to think critically, scrutinise evidence and investigate the structural problems that permeate society – as well as the solutions. You will be exposed to journalism at the cutting edge of digital technologies. State-of-the-art facilities, including television and radio studios and editing suites, ensure our graduates are practice and academically ready for the industry. In-depth knowledge of current and emerging media practice, from investigative journalism and photography to digital and audio-visual production, equips Monash graduates with the skills to create stories that reach everywhere, inspire action and push limits.

Monash graduates are trailblazers in Australian media and beyond: our global approach, including a field trip abroad, gives you the edge in a competitive international market. You will join a community of award-winning academics and peers from all areas of the industry. We will empower you to build on prior study, go deeper and open up vast potential careers in media and research, including PhD study. Our graduates learn how to conduct research, read the media critically, write clearly, and make compelling evidence-based arguments.

Media leads the charge in a rapidly changing world, and Monash graduates are poised to be the innovators who shape what journalism will become. As leaders, graduates of the program make a difference to the world by telling the stories the public need to know.

### Structure
The course is structured in five parts: Part A. Foundation studies, Part B. Core studies, Part C. Applied studies, Part D. Professional practice studies and Part E. Elective studies 

A research pathway is also available for students seeking eligibility to apply for HDR studies.

Part A. Foundation studies

These studies provide you with foundation knowledge and skills in the field of global media and communications at graduate level.

Part B. Core studies 

These studies will immerse you in journalism studies at graduate level. Through a combination of academic and practice-based work, you will gain a solid foundation in creating works of journalism from mastering the written word in print through to video, audio, photography, digital production, investigative and data - in metropolitan, regional and international contexts.

Part C. Applied studies

The focus of these studies is professional or scholarly work that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development.

Part D. Professional practice studies 

Designed in association with industry experts, select from this suite of professional enhancement offerings to build essential competencies for your career pathway.

Part E. Elective studies

Select from a range of options designed to enhance specific knowledge and skills in journalism and related fields. 

Master's entry points

Depending on prior qualifications you may receive entry level credit (a form of block credit) which determines your point of entry to the course:

  * If you are admitted at entry level 1 you complete 96 credit points, comprising Part A, Part B, Part C, Part D and Part E.
  * If you are admitted at entry level 2 you complete 72 credit points, comprising Part B, Part C, Part D (6 credit points) and Part E (24 credit points).
  * If you are admitted at entry level 3 you complete 48 credit points, comprising Part B, Part C, and Part D (6 credit points).

Note: If you are eligible for credit for prior studies you may elect not to receive the credit and complete one of the higher credit-point options. 

Course progression maps

If you are eligible to enrol in the 1.5-year entry point, you have the option of completing this course intensively over a 12-month period by following the intensive course progression map.

### Course intended learning outcomes
On successful completion you will be able to:
**1.**
analyse and critically evaluate journalism theory and its application in professional practice and scholarship;
**2.**
exercise professional journalism ethics, in the pursuit of truth, accuracy and fairness, and in service of the democratic process and the public right to know as manifested by public interest journalism;
**3.**
critically analyse the history, role and function of journalism and the news media in local, national, regional and global contexts;
**4.**
utilise independent research and reporting skills in a range of generic and digital media technologies and formats, for a diversity of people and cultures in a global society;
**5.**
enter or continue professional practice in the news media with the required expert knowledge and specialist skills to shape the profession during a time of significant technological and societal change.

### Progression to further studies
Successful completion of this course may provide a pathway to a graduate research degree if you complete the research pathway.

Master's accelerated pathway

### AHEGS
The Master of Journalism is a postgraduate course. It is taught in English and normally takes two years of full-time study or part-time equivalent to complete. The course emphasises high level skills in research and reporting for all media - print, online, audio and video - combined with critical analysis of the role of the media in contemporary society. Graduates will be able to demonstrate strong professional research and reporting skills in a range of media technologies and formats. In addition, they will demonstrate an understanding and ability to contribute to the important role of professional and ethical journalism in the service of the public right to know and democratic process and an effective understanding of the role of journalism and the media in local, national, regional and global contexts. The Master of Journalism is a Level 9 Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) qualification. The minimum requirements for admission are set out in the Monash University (Academic Board) Regulations.

### Overview
Our world is being shaped by big questions about global justice, war, peace, social movements, and inter-state relations. These questions help define what this Master of International Relations is all about. In short, this course offers you a window into the diverse and dynamic world of politics in the 21st century.

Alongside a suite of core units covering key issues in International relations, you will have the opportunity to curate your learning towards your own interests and career pathway by selecting units from key international relations specialist knowledge areas including:  Global business and management, Global justice and development, and Global security. 

This course provides you with a comprehensive knowledge of international affairs, grounded in the key fundamental debates framing global politics and driven by in-depth empirical analysis. Through this, you will be able to cut through the complexity of global politics by acquiring the analytical perspectives and skills needed to see both the 'bigger picture' and comprehend detailed aspects of specific issues.

Subject to conditions, you will have the opportunity to pursue research interests in a number of areas, providing you with a potential pathway into a Higher Degree by Research. Our graduates have gone on to a broad range of occupations and have been employed by the likes of the United Nations, the Australian Government, and non-governmental organisations such as the International Red Cross.

### Structure
The course is structured in four parts: Part A. Core studies, Part B. Applied studies, Part C. Professional practice studies and Part D. Elective studies.

A research pathway is also available for students seeking eligibility to apply for graduate research studies.

Part A.  Core studies

These studies draw on best practices within the broad realm of international relations practice and research exploring the theoretical, analytical, economic, and security dimensions of global politics. 

Part B.  Applied studies

These studies cover key issues in diplomacy and global political economy, gender, peace and security, global migration, and political violence and counter-terrorism. Additionally you will undertake professional or scholarly work that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development.

Part C.  Professional practice studies

Designed in association with industry experts, select from this suite of professional enhancement offerings to build essential competencies for your career pathway.

Part D.  Elective studies

Choose from a variety of units to further your knowledge of your chosen specialist knowledge areas, or world politics more broadly.

Master’s Entry Points

Depending on prior qualifications you may receive entry level credit (a form of block credit) which determines your point of entry into the course:

  * If you are admitted at entry level 1, you complete 96 credit points, comprising Part A, Part B, Part C, and Part D.
  * If you are admitted at entry level 2, you complete 72 credit points, comprising Part A, Part B, Part C (6 credit points) and Part D (18 credit points).
  * If you are admitted at entry level 3, you complete 48 credit points, comprising Part A and Part B.

A research pathway is also available for students seeking eligibility to apply for graduate research studies.

Note: Students eligible for credit for prior studies may elect not to receive the credit and complete one of the higher credit-point options.

The Master of International Relations is a postgraduate award. The course is taught in English and normally takes two years of full-time study or four years of part-time study and successful completion requires a combination of core units, which includes either 24 points of thesis units or a 12 point research-based coursework unit, and up to 48 points of electives. The program is designed to enable graduates in international relations, politics or cognate disciplines to explore the many issues raised by the rapidly changing nature of the contemporary international system. It is particularly suitable for those interested in pursuing careers in areas such as government, diplomacy, business, teaching and journalism. It pays particular attention to relationships among major powers and to developments in Australia's regions. The Master of International Relations is a Level 9 Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) qualification.  The minimum requirements for admission are set out in the Monash University (Academic Board) Regulations.

## Master of International Relations and Master of Journalism
##### A6011

### Overview
This is a double degree course leading to two master's degrees: the Master of International Relations and the Master of Journalism. Our world is being shaped by big questions about global justice, war, peace, social movements and inter-state relations. These questions help define what this double degree course is all about. In short, this course offers you a window into the diverse and dynamic world of politics in the 21st century. This course provides an entry-level qualification for a professional journalism career, and a mid-career course for working journalists seeking to extend their expertise and refresh the intellectual basis of their practice. The journalism component is designed to ensure you will make an excellent contribution to their profession using a full range of media technologies and the course has a particular focus on public interest and investigative journalism.

Alongside a suite of core units covering key issues in International Relations, you will have the opportunity to curate your learning towards your own interests and career pathway by selecting units from key international relations specialist knowledge areas including:  Global business and management, Global justice and development, and Global security.

This course provides you with a comprehensive knowledge of international affairs, grounded in the key fundamental debates framing global politics and driven by in-depth empirical analysis. Through this, you will be able to make sense of the complexity of global politics by providing the analytical perspectives and skills needed to see both the 'bigger picture' and comprehend detailed aspects of specific issues.

Journalism studies focuses on finding the truth and telling the story and plays a crucial role in scrutinising and holding to account those in power and influence.

Graduates have also found careers in news media, and have become young entrepreneurs establishing their own firms both in Australia and abroad.

## Master of International Sustainable Tourism Management
##### A6012
##### 96 credit points
You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
Sustainability represents an increasingly influential facet of tourism planning, development, governance and management, encompassing a diversity of sectors as the industry continues to expand globally. The United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) is also forecasting that the growth rate for emerging economies will be double the rate of advanced economies in the years leading to 2030 and that a sustainable industry can therefore play a significant role in the achievement of development goals. 

Effective planning and policy making for international tourism, and for the management of environmental, socio-cultural and economic consequences is critical. There is a growing demand for well-qualified managers who not only have a broad and deep understanding of global business activity and market based solutions, but a clear insight into the consequences of planning and policy-making on the environment, society, culture and the economy. 

This course looks at the driving forces behind the global tourism economy and how tourism can be compatible with the development of sustainable organisations, urban and rural development/regeneration, natural resource management, as well as the diversifying benefits from international and domestic tourism. It facilitates the development of skills and techniques to develop tourism policies and practices in a global setting and to manage tourism development and enterprises in the direction of more sustainable practice. 

You will be encouraged to take part of your studies overseas either on a field school or exchange in order to broaden your understanding of the international market. The course provides the opportunity to attend a partially funded intensive field school to study the patterns of development within an emerging economy in the Asia-Pacific such as Fiji and Vietnam.

You will undertake a fully funded overnight industry integrated field schools in Sydney, Hobart and regional Victoria to understand the dynamics of the contemporary industry during their first year of study.

## Master of International Relations (Double Masters with Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

### Overview
This international double master's program enables you to complete the requirements of the Monash Master of International Relations as well as a second degree with Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU).

You will study one year at Monash University in Australia and one year at the partner university. On successful completion of the academic program at Monash and the academic program at the partner university, you will be eligible to graduate with the degrees from both institutions, awarded separately.

This double degree course is subject to maximum quotas for each partner university. If you are interested you must inquire directly to the course coordinator for Master of International Relations in the Faculty of Arts at Monash, and if eligible, will be invited to apply.

Our world is being shaped by big questions about global justice, war, peace, social movements, and inter-state relations. These questions help define what this Master of International Relations is all about. In short, this course offers you a window into the diverse and dynamic world of politics in the 21st century.

Alongside a suite of core units covering key issues in International Relations, you will have the opportunity to curate your learning towards your own interests and career pathway by selecting units from key international relations specialist knowledge areas including:  Global business and management, Global justice and development, and Global security. 

This course provides you with a comprehensive knowledge of international affairs, grounded in the fundamental debates framing global politics and driven by in-depth empirical analysis. Through this, you will be able to make sense of the complexity of global politics by providing the analytical perspectives and skills needed to see both the 'bigger picture' and comprehend detailed aspects of specific issues.

Subject to conditions, you will have the opportunity to pursue research interests in a number of areas, providing you with a potential pathway into a Higher Degree by Research. Our graduates have gone on to a broad range of occupations and have been employed by the likes of the United Nations, the Australian Government, and non-governmental organisations such as the International Red Cross.

### Overview
This is a double master's program jointly offered by Monash University, Australia and the University of Warwick, United Kingdom. This international double master's program will allow you to complete, via 2.5 years, the full requirements of the Monash Master of Journalism degree, plus the full requirements of one of the Master of Arts degrees taught in the department of Politics and International Studies (PAIS) at University of Warwick. If you commence the program at Warwick, you may be able to complete in a minimum of two years, due to the alignment of semester/term schedules.

The program will conclude with a joint research project, addressing the two degree study areas. You may commence your studies either at Monash or at Warwick and also have the choice of mobility in the dissertation period so that you can return to the institution at which you started or continue at the other institution.

##### A6023

### Overview
This international double master's program enables you to complete the requirements of the Monash Master of Interpreting and Translation Studies (MITS), as well as a second degree with one of the following universities:

  * Jean Moulin Lyon III (Specialising in business and legal translation, French)

  * Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (Specialising in interpreting and translation/Japanese)

  * Università di Bologna (Specialising in specialized translation)

In each case, you will study one year at Monash University in Australia and one year at the partner university.  On successful completion of the academic program at Monash and the academic program at the partner university, students will be eligible to graduate with the degrees from both institutions, awarded separately.

This double degree course is subject to maximum quotas for each partner university. If you are interested you must inquire directly to the course coordinator for MITS in the Faculty of Arts at Monash, and if eligible, will be invited to apply.

The Master of Interpreting and Translation Studies is aimed at students with advanced bilingual proficiency.  It seeks to develop your skills in translation and interpreting from/to English and another language, and your awareness of practical and theoretical approaches to translation/interpreting practice and studies.

You will gain a foundation in theories of translation and interpreting and receive training in research in the field. Upon completion of this course, you will be able to conceptualise translation/interpreting studies as an academic discipline in its historical, cross-disciplinary and intercultural context.

Students who wish to be recommended for National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters (NAATI) accreditation in Australia on completion of the course would need to sit (and achieve the required result in) final exams after completion of the second year of the degree. Contact the course coordinator for details

The course is structured to represent your studies at Monash University and your studies at your chosen partner institution.

All students commence the program at Monash, Australia and complete the program in Jean Moulin Lyon III, France. Following the completion of the academic program at Monash comprising 48 credit points (one year full-time) of study toward the Master of Interpreting and Translation Studies, you will travel to France to complete a further 60 ECTS (one year full-time) of study toward the JMLIII Master of Foreign Languages.

Partner institution - Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (KCUFS)

All students commence the program at Monash, Australia and complete the program at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Japan. Following the completion of the academic program at Monash comprising 48 credit points (one year full-time) of study toward the Master of Interpreting and Translation Studies, you will complete a further 20 KCUFS points (one year full-time) of study toward the KCUFS Master of Interpreting and Translation Studies.

Partner institution - Università di Bologna (Bologna)

All students commence the program at their home institution and complete the program at the partner institution.

For Monash students, following your first year of study toward the Monash Master of Interpreting and Translation Studies, you will travel to Italy to complete a further 60 ECTS of study toward the Università di Bologna Master of Specialized Translation.

For Università di Bologna students, following your first year of study toward the Master of Specialized Translation, you will travel to Monash to complete a further 48 credit points of study toward the Monash Master of Interpreting and Translation studies.

Students commencing at Monash

Your Monash studies will focus on foundational and core studies that include the theory and practice of translation and interpreting, familiarising you with current research models and methodologies in translation studies.

Your studies will draw on best practices within interpreting and translation fields, providing intensive language-specific practice in written and oral transfer skills at a level required for certification by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters (NAATI). In addition to the relevant theoretical frameworks, the core studies will also provide you with the discourse analysis, ethical and professional frameworks that are essential for professional interpreting and translation practice.

Students commencing at Bologna

Your Monash studies will draw on best practices within interpreting and translation fields, providing intensive language-specific practice in written and oral transfer skills at a level required for certification by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters (NAATI). In addition to the relevant theoretical frameworks, the core studies will also provide you with the discourse analysis, ethical and professional frameworks that are essential for professional interpreting and translation practice.

You will also undertake professional or scholarly work that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development and develop advanced skills in specialised fields of translation.

## Master of Public Policy

### Overview
This comprehensive degree builds practical knowledge and essential skills for international careers in policy making and management across the spectrum of public sector activities. The multi-disciplinary program develops understanding of the processes of policy formation, the delivery of policy programs, and the political and structural realities that can impact on decision-making. The course combines a focus on foundation knowledge and understanding of critical issues in public policy, governance, and policy analysis and evaluation.

You can choose to specialise in global studies which will develop your policymaking skills and knowledge in international contexts, or policy studies from which you can study a choice of streams including: Criminology, Cultural and creative industries, Diplomacy and international trade, Family violence prevention, Global Migration, Health and social policy, Organisational leadership, Public finance, Regulatory policy, Sustainability and the environment, Transport and Urban policy.

Participants are equipped for careers in public, not-for-profit and private organisations engaged in policy development and program delivery at all levels of government and between governments.

### Course duration (full time)


### Structure
The course comprises 96 credit points structured into four parts: Part A. Core studies, Part B. Professional practice studies, Part C. Applied studies, and Part D. Specified elective studies.

A research pathway is also available for students seeking eligibility to apply for HDR studies.

Part A. Core studies 

These studies will introduce you to public policy theory and practice at an advanced graduate level. Throughout these studies, you will gain practical knowledge and skills that will provide a solid foundation for the specialist studies units undertaken in the program.  

Part B. Professional practice studies

Designed in association with industry experts, select from this suite of professional enhancement offerings to build essential competencies for your career pathway

Part C. Applied studies

The focus of these studies is professional and project work, focused locally or globally, that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development. In this part of the program you can also undertake higher level research.

Part D. Specified elective studies

The focus of these studies is to develop your expertise in a specialisation: Policy studies or Global studies. These will provide you with the knowledge and skills needed for the capacity to work and communicate across the borders of context or discipline.

Master's entry points

Depending on prior qualifications you may receive entry level credit (a form of block credit) which determines your point of entry to the course:

  * If you are admitted at entry level 1, you complete 96 credit points, comprising Part. A, Part. B, Part. C and Part. D.

The Master of Public Policy is a postgraduate degree. The course is taught in English and normally takes two years of full-time study or four years of part-time study or equivalent. Graduates develop expert critical knowledge and skills to deal with management and policy analysis issues across the spectrum of public sector activities. The Master of Public Policy is a Level 9 Australian Qualification Framework (AQF) qualification. The minimum requirements for admission are set out in the Monash University (Academic Board) Regulations.

The Master of Global Public Policy is a postgraduate degree. The course is taught in English and normally takes two years of full-time study or four years of part-time study or equivalent. Graduates develop expert critical knowledge and skills to deal with management and policy analysis issues across the spectrum of public sector activities. Graduates have acquired specialist knowledge in policymaking across international contexts and are able to work in cross-cultural settings on interconnected global issues. The Master of Global Public Policy is a Level 9 Australian Qualification Framework (AQF) qualification. The minimum requirements for admission are set out in the Monash University (Academic Board) Regulations.

## Master of Strategic Communications Management
##### A6030
##### 96 credit points
You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
The Master of Strategic Communications Management provides you with the professional skills, specialist knowledge and key capabilities relevant to career pathways in a wide range of strategic communication related fields. This industry focused degree develops core competencies in critical areas of advocacy and persuasion, public relations and crisis communications, audience research and data analytics which can be applied to the government, corporate, not-for-profit and community sectors. Drawing on best practices locally and globally, graduates will be equipped to build effective and ethical communication strategies across local and international cultures and be responsive to a digitally integrated world. Taught by a combination of leading academics and practitioners in the field, you can also choose to develop deep knowledge in key elective fields including policy communication, health communication, communication for sustainability and environment, communication for social change and development and management, leadership and entrepreneurship.

### AQF level
Level 9 - Master's Degree (Coursework)

099501E

### Structure
The course is structured in four parts: Part A. Core studies, Part B. Applied studies, Part C. Professional practice studies and Part D. Elective studies.

Part A. Core studies

These studies draw on best practices within the broad realm of strategic communications studies practice and research to further your understanding of strategic communications management both locally and globally. Studies focus on the challenges posed and how communication management can play a key role in an increasingly global and digital environment.

Part B. Applied studies

As tomorrow’s leaders, you will develop a suite of transferable professional skills to respond effectively to pressing strategic communications issues. You will learn the skills to engage necessary stakeholders to allow them to effectively formulate, influence and evaluate communication practices in a variety of professional contexts. The focus of these studies is professional or scholarly work that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development. You will have the skills to work together to analyse and, identify best practices and understand and evaluate their transferability, and develop innovative and impactful solutions with real world applications.

Part C. Professional practice studies

Designed in association with industry experts, select from this suite of professional enhancement offerings to build essential competencies for your career pathway.

Part D. Elective studies

Elective units enable you to further your knowledge of your chosen focus, or strategic communication management more broadly. 

Master's entry points

Depending on prior qualifications you may receive entry level credit (a form of block credit) which determines your point of entry to the course:

  * If you are admitted at entry level 1 you complete 96 credit points, comprising Part A, Part B, Part C and Part D.

  * If you are admitted at entry level 3 you complete 48 credit points, comprising Part A (24 credit points), Part B, and Part D (12 credit points).

Note: If you are eligible for credit for prior studies you may elect not to receive the credit and complete one the higher credit-point options.

This international double master's program enables you to complete the requirements of the Monash Master of Strategic Communications Management as well as a second degree with Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU).

The Master of Marketing and Digital Communications provides you with the professional skills, specialist knowledge and key capabilities relevant to career pathways in a wide range of strategic communication and marketing related fields. This industry focused degree is designed for those seeking cutting edge theoretical knowledge and problem solving skills in marketing and develops core competencies in critical areas of advocacy and persuasion, public relations and crisis communications, audience research and data analytics which can be applied to the government, corporate, not-for-profit and community sectors. This comprehensive degree builds practical knowledge and essential skills for international careers in policy making and management across the spectrum of public sector activities. ### Course intended learning outcomes
On successful completion you will be able to:
**1.**
devise and deliver innovative solutions to policy-related challenges employing advanced critical thinking, evaluation and research skills;
**2.**
demonstrate leadership capacity in cross-cultural competence, effective team engagement, and ethical values.
**3.**
employ expert knowledge and specialist skills in policy development, research, management and evaluation to enable discipline based solutions relevant to diverse business, professional and public policy communities;
**4.**
communicate policy-related matters and advocacy effectively and perceptively in a range of formats to professional and non-professional audiences;

### AHEGS
The Master of Public Policy and Management is a postgraduate degree. The course is taught in English and normally takes one and a half years of full-time study or three years of part-time study or equivalent. Graduates develop expert critical knowledge and skills to deal with management and policy analysis issues across the spectrum of public sector activities. The Master of Public Policy and Management is a Level 9 Australian Qualification Framework (AQF) qualification. The minimum requirements for admission are set out in the Monash University (Academic Board) Regulations.

## Master of Public Policy (Double Masters with O.P. Jindal Global University)
##### A6037
##### 96 credit points
You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
This international double master's program enables you to complete the requirements of the Monash Master of Public Policy as well as a second degree with O.P Jindal Global University (JGU).

You will study at Monash University in Australia and at the partner university. On successful completion of the academic program at Monash and the academic program at the partner university, students will be eligible to graduate with the degrees from both institutions, awarded separately.

This comprehensive degree builds practical knowledge and essential skills for international careers in policy making and management across the spectrum of public sector activities. The multi-disciplinary program develops understanding of the processes of policy formation, the delivery of policy programs, and the political and structural realities that can impact on decision-making. The course combines a focus on foundation knowledge and understanding of critical issues in public policy, governance, and policy analysis and evaluation with the choice of a broad range of policy specialisations including: Criminology, Cultural and creative industries, Diplomacy and international trade, Family violence prevention, Global Migration,  Health and social policy, Organisational leadership, Public finance, Regulatory policy, Sustainability and the environment, Transport and Urban policy. Participants are equipped for careers in public, not-for-profit and private organisations engaged in policy development and program delivery at all levels of government and between governments.

### Structure
The course is structured in five parts. Part A. Core studies, Part B. Professional practice studies, Part C. Applied studies and Part D. Specified elective studies and Part E. Partner studies 

Part A. Core studies 

These studies will introduce you to public policy theory and practice at an advanced graduate level. Throughout these studies, you will gain practical knowledge and skills that will provide a solid foundation for the specialist studies units undertaken in the program.  

Part B. Professional practice studies

Designed in association with industry experts, select from this suite of professional enhancement offerings to build essential competencies for your career pathway

Part C. Applied studies

The focus of these studies is professional and project work, focused locally or globally, that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development. In this part of the program you can also undertake higher level research.

Part D. Specified elective studies

These studies will provide you with the knowledge and skills needed for the capacity to work and communicate across the borders of context or discipline.

Part E. Partner studies
On transferring to the partner institution (JGU), students will complete studies equivalent to 48 credit points of units in the Monash Master of Public Policy as per the requirements of the JGU course.

## Master of International Development Practice (Double Masters with Tata Institute of Social Sciences)
##### A6038
##### 96 credit points
You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
This international double master's program enables you to complete the requirements of the Monash Master of International Development Practice as well as a second degree with Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS).

You will study at Monash University in Australia and at the partner university. On successful completion of the academic program at Monash and the academic program at the partner university, students will be eligible to graduate with the degrees from both institutions, awarded separately.

Equitable and sustainable human development remains a pressing global concern. Complex socio-political, health, economic, cultural, humanitarian, and ecological challenges contribute to extreme poverty, reduced human development, fragile governance and environmental vulnerability affecting the well-being of millions of people worldwide. These complex, multidimensional challenges require adaptable professionals with the practical skills and analytical capacity to strategically and ethically address them at community, national and global levels. Our graduates can adapt rapidly to changing circumstances while understanding that at the core of development practice are enduring principles of social justice, equity, inclusion, and sustainability

The Master of International Development Practice offers a multi-disciplinary, applied approach to the theory and practice of sustainable human development. Delivered by specialists across the humanities and social sciences, medicine, business and economics, education and law Faculties, the program delivers rigorous research training alongside the critical and practical skills of project design and management and leadership skills. 

You may choose to focus your electives in one of the following areas:

  * democracy, justice and governance

  * gender, peace and security

  * crisis, change management and leadership

  * sustainable resource management

  * sustainable economies

  * global migration

Graduate employment opportunities may include local and international non-government organisations, human rights advocacy, aid agencies, government, social enterprise, corporate social responsibility, the business sector, universities, community organisations, and international institutions such as the United Nations,  World Bank and International Migration Organisation.

### Structure
The course is structured in four parts. Part A. Core studies, Part B. Applied studies, Part C. Elective studies and Part D. Partner studies.

Part A. Core studies 

These studies will immerse you in international development practice at graduate level and draw on best practices within the broad realm of international development theory, practice and research to address questions ranging from the causes of inequality and disparity, evolving aid and development thought and practice, to the impact of politics, economics, culture, history and natural resources human development.

Part B. Applied studies  

The focus of these studies is professional or scholarly work that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development.

Part C. Elective studies

Select from a range of options designed to enhance specific knowledge and skills in international development practice and related fields. 

Part D. Partner studies

On transferring to the partner institution (Tata Institute of Social Sciences), students will complete studies equivalent to 48 credit points of units in the Monash Master of International Development Practice as per the requirements of the TISS course.

##### A6039

You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
The Master of Marketing and Digital Communications provides you with professional skills, specialist knowledge and key capabilities relevant to career pathways in a wide range of strategic communication and marketing related fields. This industry focused degree is designed for those seeking cutting edge theoretical knowledge and problem solving skills in marketing and communications. It develops core competencies in critical areas of digital marketing, strategic and crisis communications, audience research and data analytics which can be applied to the government, corporate, not-for-profit and community sectors.

Drawing on best practices locally and globally, you will be equipped to build effective and ethical communication and marketing strategies across local and international cultures and be responsive to a digitally integrated world. Taught by a combination of leading academics and practitioners in the field, you can also choose to develop deep knowledge in key elective disciplines from across the Indonesia campus.

### Structure
The course comprises 72 credit points structured into three parts: Part A. Core studies, Part B. Applied studies and Part C. Discipline elective studies.

Part A. Core studies

These studies draw on best practices within the broad realm of communications and marketing practice and research to further your understanding of communications and marketing systems both locally and globally. These studies engage with theoretical and industry based perspectives to provide an understanding of how organisations can connect and engage with their different stakeholders to achieve specific communication and marketing objectives. Studies focus on the opportunities and challenges posed by the emergence of digital media, globalisation and increasing levels of cross-cultural exchange. The impact of technological change on marketing and communication behaviour will also be critically analysed.

Part B. Applied studies

The focus of these studies is professional and project work, focused locally or globally, that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development. In this part of the program you can also undertake higher level research.

Part C. Discipline elective studies

The focus of these studies is to develop your expertise in disciplines from across the Indonesia campus. These will provide you with the knowledge and skills needed to work and communicate across different industry and disciplinary contexts.

## Master of International Sustainable Tourism Management (Double Masters International)
##### A6040
##### 96 credit points
You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
This international double master's program enables you to complete the requirements of the Monash Master of International Sustainable Tourism Management as well as a second degree with Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB).

You will initially study a full year at Institut Teknologi Bandung and subsequently a further year at Monash University in Australia. On successful completion of the academic program at Institut Teknologi Bandung and the academic program at Monash, students will be eligible to graduate with the degrees from both institutions, awarded separately.

Sustainability represents an increasingly influential facet of tourism planning, development, governance and management, encompassing a diversity of sectors as the industry continues to expand globally. The United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) is also forecasting that the growth rate for emerging economies will be double the rate of advanced economies in the years leading to 2030 and that a sustainable industry can therefore play a significant role in the achievement of development goals.

Effective planning and policy making for international tourism, and for the management of environmental, socio-cultural and economic consequences is critical. There is a growing demand for well-qualified managers who not only have a broad and deep understanding of global business activity and market based solutions, but a clear insight into the consequences of planning and policy-making on the environment, society, culture and the economy.

This course looks at the driving forces behind the global tourism economy and how tourism can be compatible with the development of sustainable organisations, urban and rural development/regeneration, natural resource management, as well as the diversifying benefits from international and domestic tourism. It facilitates the development of skills and techniques to develop tourism policies and practices in a global setting and to manage tourism development and enterprises in the direction of more sustainable practice.

They will immerse you in cultural and creative industries studies and provide you with the opportunity to apply specialised understanding of the field in real world settings. They draw on best practices within the broad field of cultural and creative industries studies practice and research to further your understanding of the complex ecosystem in which cultural and economic goals and dynamics combine in ways that transgress traditional disciplinary and policy boundaries.

Part D. Applied studies - Cultural and Creative Industries
The focus of these studies is professional or scholarly work that can contribute to a portfolio of professional development.

This course is structured in four parts: Part A. and Part B. focus on Master of Public Policy and Management studies. Part C. and Part D. focus on Master of International Relations studies.

Part A. Core studies - Public Policy and Management

These studies will introduce you to public policy theory and practice at an advanced graduate level. Throughout these studies, you will gain practical knowledge and skills that will provide a solid foundation for the specialist studies units undertaken in the program. 

Part B. Specified elective studies - Public Policy and Management

The focus of these units is to develop your expertise in public policy and management studies. These studies will provide you with the knowledge and skills needed for the capacity to work and communicate across the borders of context or discipline.

Part C. Core studies - International Relations

These studies draw on best practices within the broad realm of international relations practice and research exploring the theoretical, analytical, economic, and security dimensions of global politics.

Part D. Applied studies - International Relations

These studies cover key issues in diplomacy and global political economy, gender, peace and security, global migration, and political violence and counter-terrorism.

## Master of Arts Research Training
##### A7001
You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
Enrolment in a master's by research degree involves the independent investigation of a research problem that has been formulated by you as the student. It is expected that the research you undertake will make a contribution to the discipline in which you are enrolled by applying, critiquing, analysing or interpreting that knowledge in ways that facilitate pathways for further learning. You will be supported in your research by a supervisory team.

### AQF level
Level 9 - Master’s Degree (Research)
### CRICOS code
102761K
### Post-nominals
MA Research Training
### Course duration (full time)


### Structure
This course is structured in two parts. Part 1: completion of mandatory coursework units (totalling 24 credit points) in semester one of enrolment. Part 2: an original research and thesis (or equivalent) of 20,000-25,000 words.

Course requirements

You must, in consultation with and under the direct supervision of a member/s of the academic staff:

  * carry out a program of research on an agreed topic approved by the Faculty in your chosen discipline for a specified period, including attending and/or presenting at seminars and other related activities as indicated by the Faculty
  * successfully complete coursework units (totalling 24 credit points) in semester one of enrolment which will guide you through the methodological and research dimensions of your project. 

Part 1: Completion of mandatory coursework totalling 24pts in first semester. 

Research Focused Units: 

Core: APG5155 (APR5155) Designing Research in the Humanities and Social Sciences (12pts)

Choice between: 

(i) APG5127 (APR5127) Advanced Methodologies in the Humanities and Social Sciences (12pts)

OR

(ii) APG5126 (APR5126) Practice-based research: Design, methods and modes of representation (12pts)

Part 2.: Submit for assessment a thesis of 20,000-25,000 words on the program of research which meets the requirements of the examiners. Submission of a thesis including published works may be permitted.

In the following specialisations, non-traditional research outputs are to be submitted in lieu of a thesis:

a. Creative Writing - a piece of creative writing of not more than 15,000 words with an accompanying exegesis of not more than 10,000 words.

b. Music - a creative folio of musical works of 45 minutes with an accompanying exegesis of not more than 10,000 words.

c. Theatre Performance - a performance project of a minimum of 45 minutes with an accompanying exegesis of not more than 10,000 words.

Research topics are available in most of the faculty's areas of research strength, depending on supervision and resource availability. For mode detail, refer to the Faculty of Arts Graduate Research website. 

NOTE: students must pass all coursework units with a minimum result of 70 per cent, the assessment of which is conducted in accordance with the University's Assessment in Coursework Units policy and supporting procedures in order to proceed with the research component of the course.

### Course structure

### Course intended learning outcomes
On successful completion you will be able to:
**1.**
The course learning outcomes are aligned with the Australian Qualifications Framework level 9.
**2.**
Successful completion of the program will signify that the student has successfully completed a course of postgraduate training in research under academic supervision, and has submitted a thesis that the examiners have declared to be a contribution to knowledge and which demonstrates the student's capacity to carry out independent research.

### AHEGS
The Master of Arts (Research Training) (MRes) is an AQF level 9 degree, taught in English. This course normally takes 2 years of full time study or 4 years of part time study. The course involves regular contact with supervisors, attendance and participation in graduate seminars, submission of a thesis, and completion of 24 coursework units.

Awardees of the MRes will have fulfilled the requirements for supervised study and research at the University, including a thesis of up to 25,000 words (or equivalent non-traditional research output), which demonstrates an ability to carry out independent research and critically analyse the results. The thesis is examined by two examiners, one of whom must be external to Monash University, who are recognised experts in the field of research. The minimum requirements for admission are set out in the Monash University (Academic Board) Regulations

### Degrees awarded
Master of Arts Research Training

## Doctor of Philosophy (Practice-based)
##### A8001
You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
You will undertake your doctoral studies through the Monash doctoral program. At the core of this program is the completion of a substantial research thesis on an agreed topic under the guidance of a supervisory team. Your research training is further enhanced by professional development activities or coursework units designed to support you in your academic and professional development.

Upon completion of your doctoral studies at Monash, you will be able to demonstrate that you have successfully designed and executed a research project that makes an original and substantial contribution to your discipline. In your research journey, you will have also acquired the necessary skills and professional attributes to make an immediate and enduring impact on academia, industry, government, or community.

### AQF level
Level 10 - Doctoral Degree
### CRICOS code
117341G
### Course duration (full time)


### Structure
This course consists of:

  * a creative practice project and a written exegesis

You must, in consultation with and under the direct supervision of a member/s of Faculty academic staff:

  * carry out a program of research on an agreed topic approved by the school or centre of enrolment in your chosen discipline for a specified period, including attending and/or presenting at seminars and other related activities as indicated by the relevant School;
  * submit, for examination, a dissertation component which meets the requirements of the examiners consisting of:

   i) a written exegesis of a minimum of 30,000 words that articulates the conceptual,   methodological and aesthetic context for the creative works; AND

  ii) one of the following practice-based creative components in line with disciplinary  requirements.

Specialisations are available in the following disciplines:

Creative Writing

A major creative work of a minimum of 40,000 words which may include one or more of the following:

  * a novel;
  * a group of short stories;
  * a work of creative non-fiction;
  * a play or group of plays;
  * a sequence of poems (book length, approximately 100 pages);
  * or a portfolio of works of various genres.

Translation Studies 

A body of translated work of a minimum of 40,000 words. This may include:

  * a novel or a group of short stories;
  * a play or group of plays;
  * a sequence of poems;
  * translation of an audio-visual work or video game; or,
  * a portfolio of works of various genres

Journalism

A body of work whose length depends upon the project and genre and will be negotiated with supervisors. This may include:

  * a full-length book manuscript of journalism of a minimum of 40,000 words;
  * a full-length book manuscript of creative non-fiction of a minimum of 40,000
  * words;
  * a full-length audio journalism documentary of up to 60 minutes;
  * a series of two to five linked radio or podcast productions of up to 25 minutes
  * each that constitutes a coherent body of work;
  * a short to mid-length fiction film of up to 50 minutes;
  * a full-length video journalism documentary of up to 90 minutes;
  * a series of three to five linked video productions of up to 20 minutes each that
  * constitutes a coherent body of work;
  * multimedia journalism that represents a substantial effort in the genre;
  * a feature-length audiovisual script or screenplay of 50 to 100 pages;
  * an essay film or audiovisual essay of 50 to 90 minutes;
  * a series of three to four short (three- to 10-minute) VR or AR projects;
  * a presentation of audiovisual technical experiments that explore the
  * boundaries of new or existing media technologies.

Music:

  * a live presentation of approximately 70 to 90 minutes in duration; OR
  * a portfolio consisting of an equivalent duration in music scores, recordings, programming outcomes, video or other media as appropriate to the discipline.

Theatre Performance

  * A live presentation of approximately 60-90 minutes in duration, which is presented at a Monash University venue or an approved alternative. OR
  * a portfolio consisting of an equivalent duration in performances (live or recorded), performance texts, video or other media as appropriate to the discipline.

The total combined thesis components must not exceed 100,000 words.

### Requirements
Upon entry into the degree you will be required to complete the following:

  * Monash Graduate Research Induction (online)

  * Research Integrity (online)

  * Faculty/School/Program Induction (in person)

  * Cultural Foundations: Building your knowledge of Australia's First Peoples (online)

  * Respectful Research at Monash (online)

  * Discipline-specific training as appropriate

## Professional Certificate of Specialised Health and Legal Interpreting
##### A9001
##### 12 credit points
You are viewing the 2026 version

### Overview
In this course, you will specialise in two key areas of interpreting practice: healthcare and legal settings, which include police and court interpreting. You will gain essential knowledge and specialist language specific to these fields.

You will learn about the communication styles and discourse features of the various participants that medical and legal interpreters encounter. In healthcare, this include doctors, nurses, clinicians, mental health specialists, and patients. In legal settings, you will work with police officers, lawyers, judicial officers, prison and parole officers, as well as individuals who may lack specialised knowledge of the legal system.

The course will provide you with the the opportunity to focus on both consecutive and simultaneous interpreting, using English and other languages. You will explore interactional approaches to interpreting, along with theoretical concepts related to health and legal interpreting as emerging research fields.

## Bachelor of Business

### Overview
The Bachelor of Business will enable you to delve into the dynamic world of business. You will have the opportunity to understand what makes organisations, brands and markets function effectively and sustainably. Whether you are interested in working for a large corporation, or a not-for-profit organisation, managing a business, or becoming an entrepreneur, the Bachelor of Business will give you the knowledge and skills you need to thrive in a competitive business landscape. The course provides choice and flexibility by allowing you to develop broad business knowledge as well as specialised expertise in one or two chosen areas of business practice. It also offers you the opportunity to study overseas or undertake an internship, as well as a range of other experiences which enable you to maximise your employability at graduation. 

You will be well equipped to seek employment in both private and public-sector enterprises.

### AQF level
Level 7 - Bachelor Degree

### Post-nominals

### Structure
This is a comprehensive course, structured in four parts: 

Part A. Core studies

These studies will provide you with a broad foundation for your study of business and expose you to several business disciplines. It will contribute breadth to your knowledge of business and develop your understanding of multi-disciplinary decision making in organisations. It will also give you the opportunity to learn more about each discipline before finalising your choice of major. 

Part B. Major studies

Your major studies will provide you with a focused program of study that will develop your expertise. You will develop, apply and communicate an advanced level of understanding of the concepts and theoretical frameworks that constitute the knowledge base of your major area of study.

Part C. Capstone studies

This is designed to consolidate the knowledge and skills acquired throughout the study of your major.

Part D. Elective studies

This will enable you to further develop knowledge of your chosen major, or business more broadly, or study a second business major. Alternatively you can select units from across the University in which you are eligible to enrol.

Masters Accelerated Pathway

The Bachelor of Business offers an Accelerated Pathway option into the Master of Business, Master of Global Business, Master of Management, Master of Applied Marketing and Master of Regulation and Compliance. This Accelerated Pathway allows you to complete a master’s degree with one additional year of full-time study.

If you have completed at least 96 credit points and have achieved a high credit (65%) average, you can apply to the Course Director for the master’s accelerated pathway. If admitted to the accelerated pathway, you will use four units (24 credit points) of your elective studies (Part D) to complete master-level units from one of the destination courses.

Note: You still need to meet the entry requirement of having an overall 65% weighted average mark at the end of your degree to enter the master’s program.
